newsitem.title: USA: Bills introduced to revise N.J. energy tax reforms.
newsitem.headline: Bills introduced to revise N.J. energy tax reforms.

text.p: Two Republican leaders of the New Jersey Senate on Monday introduced bills that would revise the Whitman administration's energy tax reforms.

The administration, recognizing that vertically integrated public utilities were struggling under a competitive disadvantage, proposed eliminating the 13-percent Gross Receipts and Franchise Tax. It would replace it with the state's 6 percent sales tax and corporate income tax on profits. Independent energy producers and so-called co-generators now do not pay the tax.

Bills introduced by Senate President Donald DiFrancesco and state Sen. Peter Inverso would limit the sales tax exemption on current non-utility energy purchases to seven years. The administration proposed a permanent exemption.

The second bill would guarantee that at least $730 million would be distributed to the state's 567 municipalities. That figure is the average of recent gross tax distributions. It is a century-old tax designed to replace local property taxes for state franchised and regulated utilities.
